correctness.rationale: After affine normalization of the half-plane, the hypothesis forces \(c=\beta A\) to be real positive and \(a=(\beta B+\gamma)/c\) to satisfy \(\operatorname{Re}a\ge0\). Analyticity of \(P\) makes \(Q+a\) zero-free. For the boundary-winding lemma, a periodic argument exists because the zero-free analytic function has winding number zero; the \(\alpha=0\) case is an exact periodic-primitive identity, while for \(\alpha>0\) the smoothed-sign Stokes formula has nonnegative integrand on its support. This proves the circle \(L^1\) contraction. The Paatero–Pinchuk criterion then transfers membership from \(P\) to \(q\).
residual_risks: The proof relies on the classical Paatero–Pinchuk characterization as quoted in the source literature; no equality classification is needed.
